previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with prior Roux-en-Y gastric bypass and gastrostomy tube dependence was admitted to the bariatric surgery service after outpatient gastrostomy tube removal for abdominal pain/tenderness at the tube site and recurrent symptomatic hypoglycemia during transit, requiring oral and IV dextrose. During hospitalization she received IV fluids, glucose monitoring with dextrose as needed, nausea control with ondansetron/promethazine, and acid suppression with PPI; she developed persistent burping without other sequelae, and abdominal radiographs showed no free air or obstruction. Metabolic labs were monitored and repleted as needed, and her diet was advanced gradually from bariatric stage 1 to stage 4 with emphasis on frequent tolerated snacks to prevent hypoglycemia; outpatient follow-up was arranged for further evaluation of post-bypass hypoglycemia/nonabsorption. She was discharged home ambulatory and stable with wound care, diet, glucose-check instructions, and medication guidance (including pantoprazole and avoidance of NSAIDs).
problems: Need for prophylactic vaccination and inoculation against influenza

tolerated well with stable blood sugars.  ___

Discharge Instructions:
You were admitted to the hospital following placement of your 
gastrostomy tube.  Tube feedings were initiated and well 
tolerated.  You are now preparing for discharge to home with the 
following instructions:

Please continue infusing tube feedings 24 hours per day.  If you 
have any difficulty tolerating tube feedings (abdominal 
distention, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal pain and/or 
increased gastric residuals) or have any issues with your tube 
(unable to infuse tube feedings or flush tube, leakage around 
tube), please monitor your blood sugars closely and notify Dr. 
___ immediately. 
Also, please monitor your blood sugars routinely before and 
after meals, at bedtime and if you become symptomatic as 
directed by ___.

Please call your doctor or nurse practitioner or return to the 
Emergency Department for any of the following:
*You experience new chest pain, pressure, squeezing or 
tightness.
*New or worsening cough, shortness of breath, or wheeze.
*If you are vomiting and cannot keep down fluids or your 
medications.
*You are getting dehydrated due to continued vomiting, diarrhea, 
or other reasons. Signs of dehydration include dry mouth, rapid 
heartbeat, or feeling dizzy or faint when standing.
*You see blood or dark/black material when you vomit or have a 
bowel movement.
*You experience burning when you urinate, have blood in your 
urine, or experience a discharge.
*Your pain in not improving within ___ hours or is not gone 
within 24 hours. Call or return immediately if your pain is 
getting worse or changes location or moving to your chest or 
back.
*You have shaking chills, or fever greater than 101.5 degrees 
Fahrenheit or 38 degrees Celsius.
*Any change in your symptoms, or any new symptoms that concern 
you.
Please resume all regular home medications , unless specifically 
advised not to take a particular medication. Also, please take 
any new medications as prescribed.
Please get plenty of rest, continue to ambulate several times 
per day, and drink adequate amounts of fluids

Additionally, 
Gastrostomy(Stomach Feeding Tube) Tube Care:

Overview

Immediately following the placement of your G-tube, the dressing 
should be checked every four hours for excessive bleeding or 
discharge for the first 24 hours.

Some discomfort around the tube site is normal for the first few 
days after surgery.  If you experience severe, worsening pain, 
fever > 101.5°, nausea or vomiting, call your physician. 

The tube will be ready for use ___ days after it is inserted.  
Your physician ___ discuss the appropriate timing for 
initiation of feedings.

Basic G-tube Care

Dressing:

The area around the tube may be washed with mild soap and water.

When there is no drainage around the tube, the dressing may be 
omitted.

Prior to Feeding

The tube should be aspirated with a 60ml syringe prior to 
feeding to check for residual food.

If more that 50 ml is aspirated, stop the feeding and notify the 
physician who has ordered your formula.

Methods of Feeding
Continuous Feeding: The liquid feeding is poured into a bag and 
infused into the stomach over a 24 hour period using a pump.
